newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore bank shares rebound at the open.
newsitem.headline: Singapore bank shares rebound at the open.

text.p: Singapore bank shares rebounded in early trading on Tuesday after a strong sell-off on fears of their exposure to troubled Thai banks.
The foreign tranches of banks were hit in late Monday trade after the Thai stock exchange suspended most Thai finance and some bank stocks.

"The selling is unwarranted. We know Singapore banks have regional exposure but it is not that significant in Thailand to warrant the sell-off. We think it is a good buying opportunity at this level for the banks," said a dealer with a local firm.
The foreign tranche of OUB and UOB were top gainers, rising 30 Singapore cents each in early trading.
The Straits Times Industrials Index was up 2.53 points to 2,198.87 after 45 minutes of trading. Total market volume was 37 million units with 86 gainers against 68 losers.
Among the most active was property and construction group Tuan Sing Holdings rose 1.5 cents to S$0.665 after releasing a strong set of 1996 results.
Keppel Telecom, which announced stronger than expected 1996 results, dropped one cent to S$1.53 after announcing a rights and warrant issue to raise funds.
